summary.text: Christopher Columbus was an Italian explorer and navigator from the Republic of Genoa who completed four Spanish transatlantic voyages in the name of the Catholic Monarchs.
He developed a plan to seek a western sea passage to the East Indies, hoping to profit from the spice trade, and made landfall in the Americas on 12 October 1492.
His expeditions began a period of exploration, conquest and colonization that lasted for centuries and brought the Americas into the European sphere of influence.

facts.label: First voyage
facts.value: Left the Port of Palos in August 1492 with three ships

facts.label: First landing
facts.value: An island in the Bahamas the natives called Guanahani

facts.label: Namesake
facts.value: The Columbian exchange is named after him

items.prompt: After landing in the Caribbean, what did Columbus seem to believe about where he had arrived?

options.label: He announced to the Crown that a wholly separate continent stood there
He never clearly gave up the belief that he had reached the Far East
He proved it was the coast of Africa
He said he had reached the British Isles

items.explain: The extent to which he knew the Americas were a separate landmass is uncertain; he never clearly renounced his belief he had reached the Far East.

items.prompt: Columbus needed a king and queen to pay for a voyage west. What did it take to win their backing?

options.label: A single meeting, after which they backed him at once
A letter from the Pope ordering the voyage
Persistent lobbying in several kingdoms, and sponsorship came after the Granada War
A fleet he had already built at his own cost

items.explain: After the Granada War and Columbus's persistent lobbying in multiple kingdoms, the Catholic Monarchs agreed to sponsor a trip west.

items.prompt: Many islands on a map of the Caribbean still carry names that Columbus chose. What does this show?

options.label: Many names he gave to geographical features, particularly islands, are still in use
Local peoples adopted all of his names within a year
Later explorers renamed nearly every feature he named
He named only the mainland coast, leaving islands unnamed

items.explain: Many of the names Columbus gave to geographical features, particularly islands, are still in use.

items.prompt: Historians use one term, named after Columbus, for what followed his first voyage. What does it describe?

options.label: A treaty that divided newly found lands between two crowns
The route his ships took on every one of his voyages
A list of the colonies he founded across the Caribbean
A transfer of plants, animals, people, diseases and ideas between the Old and New World

items.explain: The transfer of plants, animals, precious metals, culture, people, technology, diseases and ideas between the Old World and New World following his first voyage is known as the Columbian exchange.

items.prompt: Western culture once idealized Columbus as a heroic discoverer. Why is he less celebrated now?

options.label: Historians proved he never sailed across the Atlantic
Greater public awareness of harm to Indigenous peoples, such as disease and enslavement
His voyages were forgotten after the Catholic Monarchs died
Records show he was never a colonial governor

items.explain: Diseases and enslavement contributed to the harm done to Hispaniola's Indigenous peoples, and increased public awareness of these interactions has led to him being less celebrated.

items.prompt: Columbus served as a colonial governor. What became of him in that role?

options.label: He was praised for gentle rule and then promoted to admiral of Castile
He kept the post for life and passed it to his son Diego
Some contemporaries accused him of significant brutality, and he was removed from the post
He gave it up on his own to return to Genoa

items.explain: As a colonial governor, Columbus was accused by some of his contemporaries of significant brutality and removed from the post.
